figures.caption: Fig. 1. Trait–payoff correlations over time across scenarios and decision rules. Rows vary the population trait scenario (baseline; high/low Extraversion, Openness, Agreeableness). Columns vary the mixing weight β that blends Agreeableness with dyad-specific history in cooperation decisions (history-dominant, balanced, trait-dominant). Within each panel, thick lines plot mean Spearman correlation ρ(trait, payoﬀ) across seeds and sizes; shaded ribbons show 95% confidence intervals (CI). Thin lines show size-conditional means by N to illustrate size robustness. The horizontal dashed line marks ρ = 0; when the Agreeableness–payoff curve first crosses 0, a vertical dotted line marks the turn. Side bars summarise end-state (t = H = 300) properties averaged across seeds and sizes: average payoff per agent (gold if positive, grey if negative), payoff inequality (normalised-by-absolute-mean Gini), and harm prevalence (share of agents with negative cumulative payoff). Insets depict the trait distributions used in each row (balanced: Beta(5, 5); scenario rows skew one trait to Beta(7.5, 2.5) high or Beta(2.5, 7.5) low). See Methods for parameter grid, payoff normalisation, and definitions of metrics.
